name: Greyholt, a week in silence
summary: A silent week for six to eight people who already have a contemplative practice. The Office morning and evening, nothing asked of you between, and rest is expected. Donation.
description:
Greyholt is a small lay community in a brick farmhouse on the edge of the fen. We keep the Office, we grow most of what we eat, and eight times a year we open the house for a silent week to people who already pray or sit regularly and want a week of it without having to arrange anything.

The frame is light. Morning prayer at seven, evening prayer at six, both in the small chapel off the kitchen, both about twenty-five minutes. Everything else is unscheduled. Guests sit in their rooms, in the chapel, in the orchard. One of us is available every afternoon between two and three for anyone who wants to speak, and otherwise nobody will approach you.

The week asks nothing of your body. We do the garden and the wood ourselves, and guests are not expected to join in or to walk or to do anything but be here. Most people sleep a great deal in the first three days. The library is warm and the chairs are good. The one walk on the property is flat and takes twenty minutes. We do this because most people who come are tired in a way they have not admitted, and a week of not being needed is the thing they actually came for.

Silence is complete from arrival to departure, including at meals. We assume you know how to hold that and do not teach it. This is not a good first silent retreat.
practical: Saturday afternoon to the following Saturday morning, eight weeks a year. No fixed cost; guests give what they can and the suggested contribution is £220 for the week. Six single rooms and one twin. Three meals daily, vegetarian, eaten in silence. Bring slippers, something to read, and something warm for the chapel. Ely is the nearest station, twelve miles; there is a bus. No mobile signal indoors.
